title: Prevent cascade of burn-rate pagers caused by transient autoscaler oscillations
creator: Maya Kapoor
description: Summary: During a capacity regression on 2025-02-08 our autoscaler aggressively spun up/down worker pools to chase bursty enqueue patterns. Short-lived capacity changes caused many routes to temporarily exceed burn-rate SLO thresholds, creating a cascade of burn-rate pagers across multiple service groups. Root cause analysis shows three contributing factors: (1) autoscaler hysteresis too low for common burst shape, (2) burn-rate alerts fire before capacity-change metadata is propagated to alerting rules, and (3) alerting recipients and aggregation are global instead of scope-local, causing duplicated pagers for the same underlying event. Goal: reduce noisy pagers from autoscaler-induced transients while preserving sensitivity to real capacity regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Pager count for burn-rate alerts during simulated autoscaler churn reduced by >=75% compared to baseline (measured on staging stress window)
Burn-rate alerts include capacity-change context (autoscaler event id and affected pool) in the first firing alert
Alerting rules apply scope-local aggregation (per-pool or per-region) to avoid duplicate pages across teams
Temporary suppression windows are implemented with bounded retries so regressions remain paged after genuine prolonged SLO breach
action_items: Add 90s autoscaler warm-up hysteresis and configurable cool-down to the node pool controller (owner: Liam Chen, estimate: 3) -> PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/realtime-autoscaler/pull/412

Tag capacity-change events into the observability stream and expose event_id on burn-rate alerts (owner: Maya Kapoor, estimate: 2) -> Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/123456789/Autoscaler+Burn+Noise
Create scope-local aggregation keys for burn-rate SLOs (pool_id, region) and update SLO rule templates (owner: Sara Martínez, estimate: 2)
Implement a 2-minute suppression window for burn-rate duplicates with exponential backoff and mandated escalation if suppression persists beyond 5 minutes (owner: Reliability Team, estimate: 3)

Reduce on-call pager recipients for transient burn-rate to a service-level rotation and route full escalation to platform SRE only after 3 successive unsuppressed firings (owner: On-call rotation leads, estimate: 1)
Add synthetic workload test to CI to reproduce burst+scale cycles and measure alert noise prior to rollout (owner: QA - Anil Gupta, estimate: 2)
Post-deploy dashboard: 'Autoscaler churn vs burn alerts' showing correlated events, alert counts, and customer-facing latency percentiles (owner: Observability - Priya Shah, estimate: 2)

notes: Trade-offs: aggressive suppression reduces noise but can delay human detection of slow capacity regressions; mitigation is bounded suppression + capacity-change tagging.
We intentionally avoid making burn-rate thresholds less strict; instead we aim to provide context and smarter routing so alerts remain actionable.
This work complements other SLO noise efforts (see ENG-21111) and will be coordinated with the dedicated capacity policy changes in ENG-20888.
